caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 238 of 2009.
lawyer: Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate, instructed by Md. Zahirul Islam, Advocate-On-Record…….For the Petitioner.
parties:
Md. Tariqul Islam……..Petitioner
Vs.
The State………Respondent
full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal at the instance of the petitioner is directed against the judgment and order dated 28.04.2009 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7370 of 2009 summarily rejecting the application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (against conviction) arising out of the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 04.01.2009 passed by the learned Judge, Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Dinajpur convicting the petitioner under Section 9(4) (kha) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 5 (five) years with a fine of Tk. 5,000/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 (three) months in Nari-O-Shishu Case No. 129 of 2008 arising out of Nababganj Thana Case No. 7 dated 11.02.2008 corresponding to G.R. No. 18 of 2008. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that on 11.02.2008 at about 1.00 p.m. the informant Hamidur Rahman (P.W.1) having returned home after completion of work searched  for his daughter Tamanna (alleged victim) aged about 3 (three) years; that the P.W.1 was informed by his mother that the convict-petitioner tried to commit rape on the minor victim Tamanna; that at the time of occurrence the convict-petitioner was caught red-handed by the neighboring people when he was trying to flee away but failed to do so and he was tortured mercilessly. Thereafter, patrol police arrested the petitioner; that the petitioner made extra judicial confession before the local people. Hence, the informant Md. Hamidur Rahman lodged the case being Nabanganj Thana Case No. 7 dated 11.02.2008 under Section 9(4)(kha) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 against the convict-petitioner. 

 4. The defence case is that the accused-petitioner is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case. No occurrence took place as alleged by the informant. At the time of trial prosecution examined 9 witnesses and they have been cross-examined by the defence but the defence examined none. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 28.04.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7370 of 2009 the petitioner preferred the instant Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Court. 

 8. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division after hearing the parties without calling the record of the case summarily rejected the application under Section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He then submits that the High Court Division without touching the merit of the case most illegally rejected the application under Section 561 A of the Code. He finally submits that the Tribunal convicted the petitioner without any legal evidence but the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the inherent power under Section 561 A of the Code can be invoked to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 10. The High Court Division having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the convict-petitioner and the materials on record found that there are positive reliable legal evidence in this case to prove the charge against the accused-petitioner. The High Court Division observed that if there is no legal evidence to sustain conviction or that the conviction is given without legal basis, it can exercise the power under Section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment and that in invoking jurisdiction under Section 561 A of the Code, there is no scope to evaluate the evidence like the appellate Court for the purpose of setting aside the judgment and order of conviction and sentence. The High Court Division found that there are adequate legal evidence on record to justify the judgment and order of conviction and sentence and it does not require further scrutiny. 

 12. In view of the clear available legal evidence, on the basis of which, impugned judgment of conviction and sentence has been passed by the Court below, we are of the opinion that there is hardly any scope to entertain the application under Section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the absence of any cogent ground for quashment, we are unable to issue any Rule in this case.”
